issues.sym: Oil pressure light, ticking or knocking, rising oil consumption, and in bad cases sudden engine failure, often on cars with stretched oil-change intervals.
issues.why: Oil in these engines could thicken into a gel-like sludge that blocks oil passages. Toyota acknowledged it with a special policy that extended coverage for sludge damage.
issues.next: If the oil light comes on or the engine knocks, stop and have it checked before driving further. Keep oil changes short and use the correct oil.

issues.sym: Slow coolant loss with no visible leak, coolant seeping near the back of the engine, overheating, or symptoms that look like a blown head gasket.
issues.why: The head bolt threads in the aluminum engine block can pull out, letting the head gasket lose its clamping force. Toyota published a repair procedure using thread inserts.
issues.next: Stop driving if the temperature gauge climbs. A shop can confirm it and install thread inserts; ignoring it can ruin the engine.

issues.sym: Hard, clunky shifts, especially the 2-3 upshift or when slowing down, and an occasional jolt when the transmission changes gear.
issues.why: Shift programming in the engine computer caused firm or poorly timed shifts. Toyota released a computer recalibration to smooth shifting.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer whether the shift recalibration has been done and have the fluid level and condition checked.

issues.sym: Oil level drops quickly between changes, low-oil warning, blue-tinted exhaust smoke.
issues.why: The piston rings can clog and let oil burn in the cylinders. Toyota ran a warranty enhancement program (ZE7) for it, which has since expired.
issues.next: Check the oil at every fill-up and top it off. Do not keep driving with low oil; a shop can confirm with an oil consumption test and discuss a piston and ring repair.

issues.sym: The dash top turns shiny and tacky, gives off glare on the windshield, or cracks.
issues.why: The dashboard material breaks down with heat and humidity. Toyota offered a warranty enhancement program (ZE6) for cracked or sticky dashboards.
issues.next: Mostly cosmetic, but glare can hurt visibility. Ask a dealer whether any coverage still applies; a dash cover is a simple fix.

issues.t: Driver's power window switch can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: Window switch that works on and off, feels sticky or hot, or a burning or melting smell from the driver's door.
issues.why: Uneven lubrication inside the master window switch could make it overheat and melt, creating a fire risk. Toyota recalled the switch.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. If you smell burning or see smoke from the door, stop using the switch and have it repaired right away.

issues.t: Accelerator pedal can be trapped by floor mat (recall)
issues.sym: Gas pedal stays down or the car keeps accelerating after you lift your foot.
issues.why: An unsecured or wrong floor mat could catch the gas pedal. Toyota reshaped the pedal, replaced mats and added brake-override software under recall.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and use only a properly secured, correct mat. If the pedal sticks, brake firmly, shift to Neutral and stop safely.

issues.sym: Sudden oil leak at the front of the engine, oil pressure warning light, and abnormal engine noise.
issues.why: The rubber section of the oil hose that feeds the variable valve timing system can break down with age and burst. Toyota ran a service campaign to replace it with a redesigned hose.
issues.next: If the oil light comes on, pull over and shut the engine off. Have a dealer check whether the updated line was installed.

issues.t: Hybrid brake actuator or brake control unit failure
issues.sym: Brake and ABS warning lights and a change in how the brakes feel.
issues.why: The hybrid's electronic brake actuator and its control unit and pedal sensor can fail. Toyota extended coverage on these parts with a warranty enhancement program (ZE1).
issues.next: Have the brakes checked promptly when the brake warning lights come on, and ask a dealer about the extended coverage.

issues.sym: A brief vibration or shudder, often around 25-50 mph under light acceleration, as the transmission locks up.
issues.why: The torque converter clutch can engage roughly. Toyota released a software update (LSC E03) and extended torque converter coverage (ZE5) if the update did not cure it.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether the software update was done. If the shudder remains, the torque converter may need replacing.

issues.t: Water leak onto airbag control module (recall)
issues.sym: Airbag warning light, heavy steering from loss of power assist, or in rare cases an airbag going off.
issues.why: A clogged air conditioning drain (spider webs were one cause) could let water drip onto the airbag control module and short it out.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. If the airbag light comes on or steering suddenly gets heavy, have it inspected right away.

issues.t: Musty or moldy smell from the A/C
issues.sym: A sour or mildew smell from the vents, mostly when the A/C first turns on.
issues.why: Moisture and debris collect on the A/C evaporator and allow mold to grow. Owners filed a class action over it, and part of it has been settled.
issues.next: Replace the cabin filter and have the evaporator cleaned. Ask a dealer about any A/C odor bulletins or settlement coverage.

issues.sym: Harsh engagement into gear when cold, abrupt 1-2 shifts, hunting for gears, or hesitation pulling away.
issues.why: Shift programming on the 8-speed automatic. Toyota issued bulletins to reprogram the engine and transmission computer.
issues.next: Ask the dealer whether the latest software update has been applied, and report it again if shifting stays harsh.

issues.sym: Check engine light, rough running, failure to start, or the engine stalling while driving.
issues.why: The low-pressure fuel pump in the tank could stop working. Toyota recalled it and replaces the pump.
issues.next: Check the VIN for these recalls and get the pump replaced. A stall at speed is dangerous, so do not put it off.

issues.sym: Brake pedal suddenly gets hard and the car takes much longer to stop, sometimes with a brake warning.
issues.why: Part of the engine-driven vacuum pump that powers the brake booster can wear and break, cutting off power assist.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. If the pedal turns hard, press much harder, stop safely and have the car repaired before driving on.
